utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber has made some inquiries, and although we should not spend too much time on it, the information we received, Ms. Pilipovic, is that the registrar was informed about a change in schedule, but the victims and witness unit was not informed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good morning. I'm now thinking -- I know I had the information at 4.00 that the witness who was planned to testify by videolink would not be able to testify, so my assessment was that yesterday we would be able to finish early. And I'm absolutely certain that I informed my associate to inform the victims and witness unit so that the other witness could prepare. I don't know whether there were any other problems along the way, and I cannot say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The victims and witness unit has informed me that they received no phone call, nor a written message. What I saw was a message which is a bit confusing as far as the time is concerned. That's the last one they received about the original schedule. As lead counsel, you should verify whether the information is sent. It happened once during the Prosecution case that we lost a couple of hours because nonavailability of a witness who was present in The Hague as far as I remember. The Chamber then said that it deplored that it happened, and it should not happen again. The same is true for the Defence. Let's then now continue. Mr. Usher -- I take it that the Defence is ready to continue the examination-in-chief of Witness DP 20. Mr. Usher --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will continue. And in order not to waste time, we will proceed although I have to say that I am not feeling quite up to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the reason the incident we just discussed, or is there any other reason? If it's -- if we should take care, then please inform us. Then if not, then I'll just accept that you have perhaps not an easy time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I just wanted to say that perhaps my voice will leave along with the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber is happy that at least the Defence, one day Ms. Pilipovic loses her voice, and only the other day then you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed. Mr. DP20, can you still hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Last time we tried to have you have a look at an exhibit which must still be with Madam Registrar. And this was D1724. And this exhibit is a report of United Nations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think we were in -- we still have to decide whether at this very moment this could be presented to the witness because the Prosecution objected. We then ordered you to first ask the witness about the document, and we have to decide whether this has been sufficiently done before we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Mr. President. I had finished by saying that we thought that we had gone far enough and that we could continue the following time with the document, and my impression was that the Prosecution wasn't objecting at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's incorrect, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But rather discuss this not in the presence of the witness, I'm very sorry that after we asked you to come in that we have to ask you to leave so soon. I hope you have some understanding for our procedural issues. May I ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Trial Chamber required the Defence to -- first to put questions to the witness before confronting him with the document as such. The questions which the Defence then put to the witness did not relate to the contents of the document, other than at one point Mr. Piletta-Zanin said "I would like to go back to the issue of the summer campaign in 1993. You said it was a large-scale offensive. Did it use artillery?" And that was it. I think that what's required, in my respectful submission, is for the Defence to ask the witness what happened, if anything, in July -- in late July of 1993 in relation to the sorts of activities which are contained in the document so that we have an account from the witness of the relevant events or lack of events which are referred to in the document, and then he can be shown -- he can be informed as to the contents of the document. I say that in order to be consistent with the ruling that you have made, as I understand it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when a witness is speaking of a large-scale operation, that says enough. And I believe that I've expressed myself in under two lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand. What I understood from your questions is that there was an offensive, and although it was not entirely clear, launched by the BiH forces. Is that what your questions were about? I mean, offensive was not located.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What the witness should tell us is whether there was or not a large-scale operation in this part of the year, in 1993. I believe his answer was yes. Now what I'd like to hear is whether what we have before us, 3.000 impacts, actually conform with reality, and this is what I want to know about, is whether this was audible, these noises of the fighting. And according to that, we would be able to conclude other things in relation to the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that I understand you well, that you take it that the evidence until now is that the BiH forces launched an attack, or...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness spoke of a considerable offensive, and I believe that the witness said that they themselves were in defensive, and therefore an offensive must have come from the side of the BiH army. I believe this is how we should interpret what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was my understanding as well. When I just briefly read what is in the 24th of July report, that is, that there was an offensive against the BiH forces which is a totally different thing, so I think that before confronting the witness whether these sounds could be heard, it should be clear from the beginning whether this would be a useful document for reference because it describes the situation, as far as I can see it at first glance, in a rather different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. President, we often saw - and this is another thing that we want to prove - is that these documents are not always correct. On several occasions, we've established that, for instance, you have a hundred outgoing shots, it doesn't mean we have a hundred incoming shots. So here, when we are speaking about an attack or an offensive that was led by the Serb forces, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. again, what we need to know is that perhaps this is a response to an activity that may have occurred just before, or even at the same time. So to base ourselves just on the text itself doesn't seem to be essential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but if you want to hear from a witness whether he could have heard or whether he heard 3.000 impacts, then at least it should be clear what impacts we are talking about. If you say well, it might be on the other side of the confrontation line, then it might become rather confusing. But let me just confer with --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If, for instance, this witness -- this is the idea. This witness is a professional soldier. He has got experience of the field, of the ground. Could he know whether, for instance, when there were at least 3.000 shots that were recorded in a specific area, could he tell us, yes or no, whether we could hear something at a distance about 2 or 3 kilometres from there. For the Defence, that seems obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as such, the Chamber does not consider that it would be inappropriate to confront the witness with this document, but it should be perfectly clear before we do so what is the issue. I think there are three issues. Do you want to elicit from the witness general information of what you could hear in a combat situation, or do you want to know specifically what he might have heard on the 24th of July, 1993? That's the first question. The second question is: If you want to ask him questions about the 3.000 impacts, it should at least be clear that we are talking about the same 3.000 impacts that he talks about, the same number of impacts as the document does, and the document speaks about impacts received on the BiH side whereas the testimony until now seems to suggest, although it's not very clear, that the firing was rather in opposite direction. Then the third question is if you want to know in general whether you could hear shell impacts at a distance of 3.000 metres, I think, or two kilometres or three kilometres, I think you can ask the witness. And as such, the document does not greatly assist in eliciting such general knowledge not related to the 24th of July and not related to the specific combat situation. So if you would first clarify exactly the issues, then ask the witness what he knows. For example, if you say we are talking about the 24th, then ask him specifically what happened on the 24th, and then of course you can confront him with the document if it's still relevant on the basis of his answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just to specify, the 24th is a very special day for a specific incident when other witnesses said that there was no combat. They didn't hear anything, so it seems normal to us to be able to go as far as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so first ask him whether he knows anything specific about the 24th, and then also clarify the other issues before you confront the witness with the document, and also that at least it's clear whether his testimony is in line with the document or is -- and then he can explain himself. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you spoke to us about an offensive which took place by the end of the month of July in 1993. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about a large-scale offensive. What did you mean by that? Could you be -- perhaps, tell us a little more about it? Could you elaborate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March 1993, there was a truce that was signed. In the beginning, it was relatively respected, and I believe that later on, in July I think, it was no longer respected. The offensive started from the inside, from the city, and also on the ring surrounding the city, on the outside of the city. That is, from the positions around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Did the troops of the VRS respond, and were they what we call artillery duels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, if I tell you that this offensive of July took place around the 24th of July, is that what you remember? So by the end of the month of July 1993; is that what you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, but I'm trying to follow your instructions so that we can see whether the witness's memory is conformed with the document. If not, we can just show him the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My instruction was not to lead the witness; my instruction was to find out from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, please, during which period in the month of July that this offensive took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second half of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I submit the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You should clarify the issues I asked you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when these combat took place, these fightings, when this offensive started, you spoke of a large-scale operation, does this mean that there were many exchanges of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when such means were used like tank shells or grenade launchers of large calibre were used, does the noise of the explosion -- can it be heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. When this fighting took place, and I'm talking about the second half of July 1993, were you able to hear, you personally, the noise of the explosion in the distance -- of the explosions in the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear explosions all over the place. It's very hard to tell whether this was far away or nearby. It's hard to assess because it's fighting. It's combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when we have strong explosions that take place, is it possible to hear it in the distance so that they are deafening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you have very strong explosion, cannon firing, grenades firing, grenades exploding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Piletta-Zanin asked a number of questions on the last occasion to the effect to -- as to the issue of what could be heard of artillery over a distance. I think the witness has given answers to those questions and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me ask you one question. If you heard explosions in the distance, could you make any distinction on whether these were explosions from the shells you fired or shells being fired from the BiH side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During combat, when there's explosion coming from all over the place it's very hard to assess because you have deafening noise from all sides. So I would say that's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Also, do I understand that you hear the explosion as deafening, that you at least hear the explosion? We agree on that I take it? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, explosion can be heard from all sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. I think if you'd like to confront the witness with the document, I think it could be done. But please keep in mind what his testimony until now is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could the witness be shown the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I know that you don't have very good knowledge of English, so you will have to concentrate on the translation. I'm going to read the first paragraph of -- paragraph about the 24th of July, 1993. And the heading "Military Activity." I'm going to ask you a number of questions, and I'd like you to remember the text that you're hearing now. [In English] "Shelling activities throughout the afternoon and past dusk. Serbian forces renewed artillery and infantry assault on BH forces defending strategic hillsides on the northeast edge of Sarajevo. The city was hit with tank, artillery and mortar shells on the hillsides of Kobilja Glava, Slatina, and Kromolj. UNPROFOR reported that the BH-controlled area of Zuc was shelled and that over 3.000 impacts were recorded. It was reported that the BH forces appeared to be holding their own but they are sustaining heavy losses." Source is New York Times, UNPROFOR. [Interpretation] Witness, I think that you remember the names that I gave you. I'm going to repeat the names because they do not appear in the English transcript. These names are Kobilja Glava, Slatina, and, Kromolj, and then the Zuc hill. Witness, this mention of 3.000 hits, does this seem to you to be in concordance with the facts that you remember about the offensive from the second half of July of 1993? I'm talking about the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. The witness was not asked in the absence of the document what recollection he had of impacts on that particular day. Therefore the effect --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two lines. Two lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is not the tone on which you speak to the other party. If you think that Mr. Ierace takes more than two lines, you can address me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the combined effect is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. DP20, do you have a clear recollection of the approximate number of shells fired on specifically the 24th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you with certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During these days, were these shells fired in numbers of hundreds or even above thousands in your recollection, general idea of the intensity of what you just called the artillery duel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The intensity was high of this artillery duel. There was a lot of exchange of grenades from both sides. I can say there were many, but I cannot tell you the exact number and it went from both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It went from both sides. Equally from both sides, or would one side fire substantially more rounds than the other would do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More or less equally. I don't know whether one side fired more than the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this document says that there were 3.000 impacts recorded on the BiH side, would a total number of, then, double, that means 6.000 impacts sound reasonable to you, or would you say, well, it was not that intensive or it was even far more intensive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, it's illogical. I don't see how someone could count 3.000 impacts. You could only subsequently have a look at how many shells were fired. But to count 3.000 explosions, in my opinion, this is impossible. What I can say is that there was a lot of firing, when there's an exchange of artillery fired throughout the dawn then it is intense. But I can't provide you with a precise number and I don't see how someone could come up with the number of 3.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for a precise number. But is it correct that there were thousands of shells, I'm talking about shells from both sides fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell me, what is the distance as the crow flies, between Kobilja Glava, and Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 3 to 4.000 metres as the crow flies, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The same question with regard to Slatina and Sedrenik, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with Slatina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And as far as Kromolj and Sedrenik is concerned, what is the approximate distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Kromolj and Sedrenik, this is closer. It's closer in relation to Kobilja Glava. Perhaps 1 to 2.000 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the distance between Zuc and Sedrenik, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zuc is further away. Perhaps 5 to 6.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, when a large number of shells, tank shells or mortar shells fall in an area which is about 2.000 metres from Sedrenik, according to your testimony, can one hear the sound that these explosions make in Sedrenik, at a distance of 2.000 metres, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you say that it is possible to hear the sound, is this something that is certain, or given all the noise that you heard on your side, and you said it was a deafening noise, was this possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm saying this on the basis of my personal experience. You can hear it, this large number creates a terrible noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Witness, before we have a look at the second document that we're going to show you in a minute, but I can always -- that I can provide the usher with now. That might be more practical if we do this. I'll give its number in a minute. But I would first like to ask you some questions about weapons and about the results of the use of certain weapons. Did you have the opportunity, Witness, of observing the results of grenade attacks? And when I said "grenade," I mean mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, did you have the opportunity of seeing the traces of a crater caused by a 120-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, did you have the opportunity of seeing the traces of a 120-millimetre shell which hit a hard surface, to be more specific, which fell on an asphalt surface?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, Witness, where did you see these traces? Could you be a little more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, when there was shelling from Hresa towards Zecja Glava. Yes, I saw this on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you saw a crater caused by a 120-millimetre shell, could you describe to the Trial Chamber what this crater looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. What kind of terrain are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm talking about a crater in asphalt.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not a very deep --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- One moment, please. Of course, the interpreters have to finish what they say. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given the guidelines yesterday, and the specific example you gave, it's my respectful submission this evidence should not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, briefly. My question to you is, does it appear from your summary that the impact of shells is an issue you are going to raise with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. First of all, this witness started his testimony before you issued your order. And secondly, we used the exact formula as in the case of the witness who preceded him. And we spoke about arms in general, and we meant the use of arms and the results of arms. This was before the order was issued. And we will be a lot more precise with other witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the basis of the order of yesterday, you should have informed the Prosecution that specifically that issue would be dealt with by this witness as well. You may proceed at this moment. The Chamber will consider whether and if what consequences this should have. But it would have been appropriate to inform the Prosecution yesterday. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you saw a crater in a hard surface, could you describe what this crater looked like. Could you describe it for the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not very deep. You can see the centre of the impact, and around -- you can see the fragments of the shell on the asphalt. It depends on where the shell came from. At one point, it's a little deeper; and in other areas, all you can see are the fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have you seen many traces of impacts such as the one you have just described for us, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during this period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, what would happen with what we call the tail-fin, the stabiliser which is at the rear of the shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the stabiliser, since when the shell hits, it goes -- it's detached. It goes astray. I don't know how many metres astray, but it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On the basis of your personal experience and with regard to 120-millimetre shells on hard surfaces, did you ever find tail-fins which were embedded in the crater, which were literally embedded in the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I now want to deal with the issue of range, rifle range. And I'm not referring to the effective distance, that is to say, the distance one can hope to attain someone, but of the technical range of a rifle. You spoke about the weapons that you received. You spoke about this the day before yesterday. For each of these weapons, can you tell us what the range, in general, was for a bullet? How far can a bullet go if it doesn't encounter any obstacles?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. Basis of the objection is whether -- is that a proper foundation has not been laid for the witness to give such opinions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness was very precise with regard to the type of weapons. He gave their production number, and he gave the calibre. And as this is a professional military man, he knows what the range of a weapon is. As a professional, I can ask him whether he knows about this, but I think that we can safely assume that he is aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed but ask in respect of each weapon whether it is knowledge based on technical information or on own experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if you can answer the question I just put to you, can you do so on the basis of your personal experience or on the basis of theoretical knowledge? What can you tell us that is based on your own personal experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, both on the basis of my personal experience and on the basis of technical knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So as a result, could you briefly reply to that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The final range of an M80 rifle, a 6.2-millimetre calibre, I can't provide you with detailed information, but it's between 4 and 5.000 metres. A light machine-gun, M72, a 7.62 millimetre, uses more or less the same kind of bullet. And then I mentioned a light machine-gun, M50 -- 53, it uses a 7.9 millimetre bullet. Its range is more distant. It has a greater range. It's between 6 and 7.000 metres. Then M84 machine-gun, 7.62 millimetre calibre, its powder charge is stronger. It has a greater range, between 7 and 8.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned M72 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You didn't give us the range of the M72. You didn't tell us about its range. But you said it was the same type of weapon. Does it have the same range as the other weapon you mentioned? What is the range of an M72?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The range of an M72 light machine-gun is like the range of the automatic rifle, since it uses the same type of ammunition. It's between 4 and 5.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, when a bullet goes astray, I'm talking about stray bullets now, and it hits someone, this is a purely speculative question, but it is within the range, for example, 3.000 metres for a range of 4, 5.000 matters, what can the effect of this bullet be on the person hit by this shot? And when I say "hit by this shot," I don't mean to say that this person was aimed at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the person would be wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So on the basis of the wound, can the person be mortally wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can we, unless you want to confer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can we provide the document that I provided a minute ago -- that I provided the usher with a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would first of all like to ask you a series of questions regarding April 1993. Do you know whether in April 1993 there was fighting, there was fighting in the zone that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And in this fighting, was it also an artillery duel that was involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when, on your side -- when you opened fire on your side, did you as a general rule open fire in the same directions? Did you aim at the same zones, the zones that were mentioned to you not long ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, in the previous document. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The places mentioned weren't in front of my zone, and we didn't open fire in the direction of those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Were you able to open fire in the direction of Sedrenik, technically speaking, in technical terms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. To go back to Sedrenik, Witness, do you know whether the BH Army was deployed in the vicinity of the Sedrenik area? Do you know whether it was also deployed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, does the name of this woods mean anything to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you, the name "Seven Woods" mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us which army was deployed there, if an army was deployed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Seven Woods' area, parts of the BH Army was deployed in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know whether in the Seven Woods' area, and I'm referring to your experience, your professional experience, your personal experience, do you know whether the BH Army that was deployed there used mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the calibre of the mortars used by the BH Army from the zone of the Seven Woods' area was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they used 82 millimetre mortar shells, mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether other mortars were used in this zone or in adjacent zones?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sticking to the two-line rule, invitation to speculate, "do you know" - leading. Primarily those two bases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a matter of speculation, I'm asking and I was careful to say that it was on the basis of your professional, personal experience, I asked the witness whether he knew mortars had been used. That was my first question; it wasn't leading. And second, I wanted to know whether he knew which mortars were used. I don't think the questions I asked him were leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP20, you were asked about the use and the calibre of mortars used by the other side in Seven Woods. You answered that question. I take it that you indicated the type of mortars of which you know they used at Seven Woods. Is that correct, the calibre? You're nodding. The nodding is not visible on the transcript for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of mortars used in areas adjacent to Seven Woods on the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you obtain that knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I obtained that knowledge from our intelligence, and after the shelling had been done, when you observed the craters, someone who was familiar with these things could recognise the calibre used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you could see on the basis of the craters what calibre was used. How would you know where these mortars were fired from?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting. I don't think your last statement reflects the evidence as translated into English, which is "someone who was familiar with these things could recognise the calibre used."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I say "you could," I did not -- perhaps I should have said, but that's perhaps my lack of precise knowledge of the English language "one." It might have been one of my next questions, Mr. Ierace. First of all, if you would see a crater, how would you know exactly where it was fired from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I knew which shell caused the crater. I know that much about craters, and the direction more or less, on the basis of the form of the crater, it is possible to determine the direction from which the shell arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And also the distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's a little more difficult. Members of the artillery determine this from their observation posts. This involves an entire procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because I was asking you about adjacent positions to Seven Woods, and I do understand that on the basis of the crater you could identify the direction where they came from, but you could not precisely establish the distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say that precisely. It's possible, but this is something that is done by a team which includes observers and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so you could not establish as facts on the basis of your own observations, just by yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not on my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then my second question is you said that - have to be precise - one could see from a crater what calibre was used. How can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, quite simply, a big calibre creates a big crater. And since I had seen craters before and I knew which shells had been used, when you would make such comparisons, well it was obviously possible to determine that a certain weapon had been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you said just by the size of the crater, one can establish what calibre is used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the first thing -- that's the simplest way. But usually there's a stabiliser in the vicinity of the crater, and everything is written on the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you establish the calibre -- may I invite you to look at me when I'm asking questions to you and not to anyone else in this courtroom. If you would have no tail-fin, could you then establish the calibre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Considering the experience and how many such craters I have seen, yes, I would be able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be -- what would a 120-millimetre crater look like on hard surface, approximate size? You may indicate with your hands, for example, what the size of the crater would be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Entire crater you see on a hard surface, it's quite shallow. But the radius would be approximately, together with the traces of the impact in the soil, would be about the size of this -- the width of this table, this desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would the parties agree that it's approximately 1 metre and 20 centimetres? Approximately. It could be 130. If you would like to measure it during the next break, that's fine. You said the impact as such would be shallow. Could you give us a further indication on...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite clear. What do you mean, more in detail?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say the crater you see is quite shallow, could you give us a depth or...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At its deepest point of the crater, it's an oval, it would be perhaps some 5 centimetres deep, approximately 5. I think you can add or subtract 2 centimetres to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would be the diameter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean of the calibre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the diameter of the hole on the hard surface.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we understand each other, considering that the hole is quite small. What I mean is that with all the other traces, all the traces that are visible, the actual hole is not very big. Its diameter is perhaps 40 to 50 centimetres --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 40 to 50 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The oval part of the hole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you now tell us how this would be for 82 millimetres? What would be the pattern of shrapnel, as I understand Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it, on the surface and what would be the crater itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately -- it would be about half the size of all the other sizes mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would it still depend on the charges used when firing the -- would that make any difference, the charges used when firing the projectile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The charge for mortar shells, the only difference is the range. So the stronger charge, the higher -- longer range. But each mortar shell follows a natural fall, so that actually the charge doesn't have any impact on the crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would the kind of detonator used have any impact, whether it's a delayed fuse or -- and what would that impact be, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mortars that I know do not have -- or we didn't use, nor did I notice the other side used these delayed fuse. From literature and from experience, I know that fuses with a delay, the effect is more intense because the shell becomes activated, so from the depth, once it's impacted. It's not activated on impact, but afterwards. That depends on the fuse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would be the effect on the crater you would see? Have you ever seen such a crater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw such a crater but not from a mortar shell. But from other artillery weapons, and then it would be far greater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank the Chamber for saving my resources. But I believe that the witness did not answer the question that I asked, so I'm going to ask the following question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said that by analysing the crater, by looking at it, visually analysing, you would be able to establish the direction it came from. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, was there, as far as you know, craters of 120-millimetres that you may have seen personally and whose direction, that is, the direction that the projectiles came from, went close to the area -- the direction it came from was close to the area known as Seven Woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You and your services during the war, were they able to draw the conclusion from that at some point that the BH Army had the use of 120-millimetre calibre weapons near the area of Seven Woods?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think every question has been leading for some time. Leading is the basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the testimony of this witness is that you could see from the pattern, the direction where a shell came from. If you are now asking not about a direction but about an area which is direction and distance, you should first explore on what basis such a determination or such an assessment could be made because until now, we heard that the witness could establish directions, not distances. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what do you know, if you know, not about the direction, but the location that these projectiles of 120-millimetres came from? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did know, but I did not establish this but the experts, artillery people who conducted observations. They had technical means to observe and to monitor, so that's how they came to this information. So they would use the topographic methods --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you now. I'm going to interrupt you. What were the conclusions that you came to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you're asking the witness what conclusions they came to first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this was "you" in plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What were the conclusions, Witness, that you arrived to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking generally, that was the method that was used, that I mentioned. We approximately came to some positions, perhaps not quite accurate, but the positions of the artillery positions --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The same one as you anticipated I was about to make previously. I take it this is acceptable hearsay in the eyes of Trial Chamber. If that is the case, let's at least hear what the hearsay was rather than the witness being invited to wed his opinion with that of the experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it has already been established. The witness said that it wasn't him but it was their expert team that was able to establish it, that he was not an expert. I believe this is already -- there's foundation here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the questions are now about what your expert's findings were. Could you then please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said already, mostly this was accurate. I cannot say it was accurate 100 per cent, but approximately we were able to determine their firing positions - with a lot of accuracy - of their mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, may I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, therefore, as a consequence, according -- following the results of the investigations, you were able or your specialists were able to -- in your army were able to establish. Could you tell us where were the 120-millimetre battery positions, if that is the case, in an area near the area of Seven Woods in a northeast area, in the northeasterly direction of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leading. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, leading is over now. Move to your next subject and call the -- call those experts who could give us full information if this -- and I take it it's an important point for the Defence. So rather use your procedural rights in a proper way in order to give the Chamber full information and the best information it needs to make its determination. The Chamber is fully aware of the importance; so therefore, make it possible for the Chamber to hear this perhaps very important evidence in such a way that it can use it at its best, that is, to establish the truth in the interest of both parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to say that I was upset by a number of the objections, by the length of the interventions of your Chamber. And I apologise if I've asked a question which is leading. However, it seems to me that it will be useful that on the basis of this witness's knowledge, we would be able to find out what were -- what was the knowledge that he knew about the source. So may I please continue with this subject without asking leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the accused could keep his voice down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we're asking for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you may proceed. Everyone knows what a yellow card means in football. You just saw a yellow card. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when I say "you," what I mean by that, you and your army. Did you know anything about the -- where this fire, these shots, came from? Did you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question is inadmissible for two reasons. "Did you know" invites too wide a range of knowledge. Secondly, it invites the witness to respond to what he knew on no specified basis as well as what he understands anyone in his army knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Ierace, sometimes you can tell the Chamber, and that's of course hearsay, of what experts would tell you if these were experts or other people nearby. I'll allow you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to continue. One thing is not clear for me, at least, is "those shots," I'm not quite sure what shots you're referring to. And would you please, each question, try to find out on what basis the witness who is, as we know, giving a lot of hearsay testimony, and that's always inevitably not of the same quality as direct knowledge. But at least that we know exactly what's the basis of his knowledge. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when I'm talking about these shots, what I mean is as I'm referring to some of the craters that you were able to examine and that you spoke to us about, and you spoke about the direction. In relation to these shots and to these craters, what did you know, if you knew anything at all, not just about the direction they came from but of the origin, the source of these shots of this fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has already said that on his own observations he could not determine the origin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we understand now the question to be about not his -- but we'll find that out, Mr. Ierace. The Chamber is fully aware at this moment of the, I would say, the character of the testimony given by this witness, and that it's not only upon the basis of his own observation and his own knowledge. And Mr. Piletta-Zanin will certainly have these issues clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As long as that's clearly understood, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask the question again. What did you know, if you knew anything, about the origin of these shots? The you is the "you" as used in French, not just you yourself but as you were able to hear in your capacity as a military expert, a military person, with the rank, experience of being there for several months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to know the direction, and later on through more analysis we would be able to know the precise location of the firing position where the shot had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You tell us about the exact location where the fire came from during this analysis and regarding this precise location, could you tell us what do you know about? What were these precise locations of the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, and just like we now mentioned the Seven Woods' area, then Sedrenik, then Babica Kuca, Babic houses, which is south from Hresa, then Babic houses, then it would be the southern slopes of Hrastova Glava, then that would be the area I know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, can we now please move on to another subject. And the subject is about orders, about instructions. Witness, could you tell us whether as far as you know instructions were given in your area for the men, for the troops, that would be in relation, first, opening of fire, and second necessary protection of civilians? What do you know about these orders or instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received orders. They were mostly verbal because we were a battalion, and we didn't get written orders. We got oral orders about opening fire in a controlled manner, so just responding to provocation. And to defend ourselves. Furthermore, in some other irregular time intervals, we had these orders repeated to us not to open fire on civilians, on civilian facilities, that we were not sure whether they were within the positions of the BH Army. Then, we received these orders in irregular time intervals. It mostly happened after we received new troops, fresh troops. And these new troops, new men, had to be warned about such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to the weapons, can you tell us, if you know, where did you get some of your weapons? Where did they come from? I'm talking generally speaking, more than on a personal level.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Army of Republika Srpska got its weapons from the warehouse of the former Territorial Defence generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I'd now like to look at the relationship with the UNPROFOR, but before that, can you tell us, did you know where did the BH Army get their weapons from? Where did they find them, if you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less in the same way. The warehouses of the Territorial Defence also existed in the places under the control of the BH army, but I know that in Sarajevo, barracks that had been under a blockade, Marsal Tito barracks, Jusuf Dzonlic barracks and so on. They stayed there and a lot of weapons remained there in those barracks. So I do know about the Marsal Tito barracks because that's where I finished my schooling, my training, so I knew about the quantities that were left there. And I was also aware of -- people who left Marsal Tito barracks, so I know what was left. Also the artillery training centre from Zadar, sometime in 1991 was actually located in the Marsal Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever hear about the use of gas, poison gas, by the BH Army? When I say poison gas, I mean combat gas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear about it, but personally I haven't seen it, nor did I hear about it from the people that I associated with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, other questions will be in relation to UNPROFOR, and some other subjects. I don't know whether this is perhaps a good moment to allow me to have a hot drink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, how much time would the Defence still need to conclude this examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think some 10 minutes or so, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I take it that the Defence will finish in 10 minutes after the break. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed, but I see that Mr. -- Yes, of course, we first have to ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom. But Mr. Ierace, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, at some stage, either now or perhaps at the end of the examination-in-chief, might I take a few moments to raise two issues. They are the extent of hearsay evidence; and secondly, the sufficiency of 65 ter summaries in relation to this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we do it at the end of the testimony since... Mr Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to turn to issues related to UNPROFOR. Did you ever have any contact of any kind during the period you were engaged in the military with UNPROFOR representatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any personal contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, were you ever aware of protests that were allegedly lodged with your battalion by UNPROFOR representatives? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, this is a purely hypothetical question. Sir, please imagine that this is something that happened. Let's imagine that something that didn't conform to the military obligations, that didn't conform to military obligations, something wrong, was committed by a member of your battalion, one of the soldiers of your battalion. In such case, what would have happened? What could you tell us about this? And this is naturally just a hypothesis. It's pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the soldier, depending on what he had done, would disciplinary proceedings would have been instituted against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: By whom, may I ask you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the commander of his unit. Depending on the seriousness of the offence, by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if the offence was very serious, what would have happened? And I'm raising the problem, the issue, of possible sanctions that might be imposed by the authorities. What do you know about this matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A court martial would be responsible for the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did this institution exist at the time that you were involved in the fighting, in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where it was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one responsible for our area was located in Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would now like to turn to a different aspect of the issues we are interested in. And it concerns the trenches. Did you see who dug the trenches on the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the distance, I could see that drenches were being dug, but I was not able to see exactly who was involved in digging them. But on the basis of the intelligence that our men obtained, on the basis of the intelligence that I had access to, we had information according to which the Serbs who had remained in Sarajevo did this, in the part of the town that was under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned information. Where did this information come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the town, obtained through intelligence work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But do you know who could receive this information? Were there any particular sources of information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the most specific source of information was from people who were leaving the town, whether in exchange or because they were fleeing. It occurred in various ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm now going to put another hypothetical question to you. If these trenches had been dug by soldiers, if these military trenches had been dug by soldiers, would you have been in a position in judicial terms to open fire on these soldiers? Would you have been in a position to open fire on these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This is a military act, digging yourself in and fortifying is a military act.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to turn back to cultural facilities or religious facilities. From your positions, were you able to see cultural -- were you able to see religious buildings which were important, for example, mosques?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was possible to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see them yourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were these mosques destroyed? Was the tower, the minaret, damaged, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the ones that I saw, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the part, in the area that you controlled, were there any other -- from the part that you controlled, were there other buildings that you could observe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Since these were the suburbs, so it was a part of the town that wasn't that populated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would now like to go back to the question of elevated sites in order to clarify things as much as possible. Could you tell this Trial Chamber which elevation points were the closest to your combat lines, the elevation points under the control of the BH Army in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in front of me there was Hrastova Glavica or Hrastova Glava, that's what it says in the map. Then there was the Borije feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Any other points? Any other sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right, Grdonj, but that wasn't really in my sight any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. In general, in general terms, what do you know about elevated points that were held by the enemy artillery in the surroundings of Sarajevo, in or around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you perhaps be a little clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know -- are you aware of the existence of any other elevated points of strategic importance which were under the control of the BH Army in the surroundings of Sarajevo or in Sarajevo itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us which points. Could you tell us the names of these points.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Zuc under the control of BH Army. Colina Kapa. Debelo Brdo, and Mojmilo. And the Hum feature is the dominant one within Sarajevo itself. These are the elevated points.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you say Colina Kapa, wouldn't it be exact to say that there were several Colina Kapas? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have Velika and Mala Colina Kapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. With regard to Mount Igman, what was the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that Igman was entirely under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my last question: According to what you know, and I'm referring to the destruction of property, of buildings, that you were able to observe yourself, in general, during which period did this destruction of property, of buildings, take place for the most part? So when did the -- when were most of these buildings destroyed or damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the course of 1992, and at the beginning of 1993. That's when the most extensive damage was inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Ierace, are you ready to start to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm ready to start, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. You'll now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, Mr. DP20.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you told us the other day that you were a sergeant during the conflict. And as I understand it -- well, first of all, is that correct, you were a sergeant throughout?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a sergeant first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that you were stationed on the part of the front line that you've indicated, at least from September 1992 until August 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many battalions were there all together in the Romanija Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five battalions, but this changed at times. Because the units were based on the territorial principle, and that zone would change. But five.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I think you told us that the name of your commander was Milan Plakalovic, is that correct? That is, the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was Vlado Lizdek the brigade commander between April 1993 and sometime in 1995? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't the battalion commander, but he was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I think I said brigade commander. And who was his predecessor as brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragoljub Milosevic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did Dragomir Milosevic cease to be the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. But around 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were the brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location changed. There were several locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's about the transcript. I heard Dragomir and Dragoljub. I think it should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you use the first name of Mr. Milosevic, did you say Dragoljub or did you use another name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragomir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter would like to add, he said Colonel Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were the brigade headquarters in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the Trebevic area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did they cease to be in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, it moved to one part to Han Derventa and part to Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean that the brigade headquarters then had two separate locations at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rear part was in Han Derventa, the logistics part, and the command part was on Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you were a professional soldier at the time the conflict broke out. What were your specialties by September 1992 in terms of your training? What weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My military occupational specialty is the infantry, so all the weapons that were in infantry in the JNA. I was familiar with this. And now in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you agree that a 60-millimetre mortar is an infantry weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you met, before September 1992, General Galic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't, not personally. We didn't meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you meet your brigade commander Dragomir Milosevic when he was brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't meet, since I was just the commander of a platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit D1789.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You drew on this map the position of part of the confrontation lines. Does that accurately depict the confrontation lines in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there any changes to those confrontation lines between September 1992 and August of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please point to the part of the confrontation line that was the responsibility of you and your platoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the commander of a manoeuvre platoon. If necessary, I was engaged along the entire line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were the responsibilities of your manoeuvre platoon specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To assist parts that were in danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you first have contact with an investigator or lawyer of the Defence team? In what month, in what year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With investigator Ms. Prodanovic, I first had contact with her in spring of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And later. I think it was in the month of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At any stage did you hand over to Ms. Prodanovic or anyone else on the Defence team any maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, concerning the relevance. No, I'll withdraw that. I thought I heard something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At any stage, did you hand over to Ms. Prodanovic or anyone else on the Defence team any maps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who had responsibility -- I'll withdraw that. You told us you were in charge of a manoeuvre platoon. How many companies permanently were responsible for various sectors of the SRK front line that you have drawn on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've referred from time to time to the right flank, and I take it that's as you stood in SRK territory looking southwest towards the city of Sarajevo. Who was responsible for the right flank immediately beyond where the front lines end on this map? Were they further companies of the Romanija Brigade, or companies of a different brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kosevo Brigade companies were responsible for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the name of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kosevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that sometimes known as the Kosevo Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the position of the front line immediately to your right flank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please take a black pen and place a short dash across --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think a blue one --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The marker --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
