utterances.text: A blue pen. And first of all, place a short dash across the SRK front line at the end of that line as you've marked it on your right flank so that we can understand when we look at the map where your battalion's responsibilities ended and the Kosevo Light Infantry Brigade's responsibilities commenced. So first of all, place the dash across the front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, continue the front line for as far as you are familiar with it for the period September 1992 to August 1994.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before these type of questions, it would be good to ask the witness whether he had any knowledge so that he can speak about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question was asked and the question was answered. He had to some extent knowledge of that, he told us. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any more. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us you were familiar with it. Have you now forgotten? Is that as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't say I was familiar with the line. You asked me whether I knew the line -- a part of the line alongside my line. I knew this because this is where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the position of the ABiH line immediately to the right of the line of your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know as much as I have already marked in. Yesterday, when I was marking, I think I went a little far. But mostly this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to the section -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, may I again ask you to look to the person who is questioning you, and not to other parties in this courtroom as I observed several times. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to the part of the front line that you marked the other day that you now say perhaps you went a little far. Just point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that I drew too long a line, but that when I was drawing the line of the positions of the BH Army, that I went across. And that's approximately this line which goes beyond my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please place a dash on the ABiH line to indicate where --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that it would be useful to show in the transcript, to describe in the transcript, what the witness indicated on the map. It doesn't appear, like Mr. Ierace says, that he's gone too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I was interrupted in the question of asking the witness to mark that point on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please mark that point on the map with a dash on the ABiH line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just a few minutes ago, you were asked about high points that were controlled by the ABiH. And one of them you said was Hrastova Glava. And I think you have placed the ABiH line very closely to that peak. Is that correct? Perhaps you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please point to the peak itself as indicated on the map. Just point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I suggest to you that in fact the ABiH line was to the west of that peak. And that peak was, effectively, no man's land. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's correct. I think you have wrong information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also mentioned the Borije feature. Could you please point to that feature on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not on the map, this feature. But I can point to it. Approximately where I'm pointing, but the map is not very clear. There should be a sharp rock that should be marked here. That would be located about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, you point immediately beneath the E in the name "Sarajevo" in large type in the vicinity of the dotted line indicating the ABiH forward position. All right. Now, you also said that -- I think it was this morning -- there were some positions in the area of Babica Kuca, Babica houses. Would you please point to that on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps you could place a cross in that position, and then alongside the cross in small print the letters "BK."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps Madam Registrar could locate P3727. They are the shelling maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you received certain information from your artillery people in relation to that location. What was that information? What were you told was at Babica Kuca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the position of the -- the firing position of the mortar unit of the BH Army was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand that according to your information, that there were no permanent positions for ABiH mortars? Was that part of your intelligence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So what was at Babica Kuca one day could be on the other side of town the next. Isn't that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. On the other side of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mortars, be they 60-millimetre, 82, or 120, are capable of fast dismantling and movement, aren't they, if that is desired by the troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But these were mortars that belonged to one of their unit. I think they belonged to the 2nd Mountain Brigade, and they moved within the area of responsibility of the 2nd Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On your side, were there mortars in permanent positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mortars that did not move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a long period of time, no. They were moved, but they stayed longer at certain positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, since one of the answers is not quite clear to me, I'd like to ask for a clarification. A question was put to you saying that "so what was at Babica Kuca one day could be on the other side of the town the next. Isn't that the position?" And then your answer was: "No, no." As I understood it, "on the other side of the town." Do you say that it did not move to another place or that it might move to another place but not at the other side of the town? It's not clear to me what your answer is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't move to the other side of the town because as I know how it was. They moved within the area of the 2nd Mountain Brigade. That is, their area of responsibility because these were the weapons that belonged to that unit. But theoretically, it is possible for them to move that far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand, your answer is they did move, but according to your knowledge, not to the other side of town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The mortars that on your side were left in the same position for lengthy periods, did that apply to 60, 82, and 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why was that? Why were they left in the same positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mortars, 60-millimetre calibre, are located on the first line, on the front line in the trenches themselves, the first line of the front. And this line was not moved. That's why they stayed there. The 82-millimetre calibre mortars and the 120-millimetre mortar, too, they had good positions that were sheltered, and they were not at risk by the fire of the opposing side artillery so they could stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You say that the 82 and 120-millimetre mortars were not at risk. Why was that that they weren't at risk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in good, steady shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that the reason that mortars are moved after they are fired, very quickly after they were fired, is to avoid return fire? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be, but that's not the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But in the case of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, I suggest to you that quite often there was no threat of return fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that you are wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that there was a gross imbalance between the SRK and the ABiH in relation to artillery and mortars. And by that I mean that the SRK had far more pieces than the ABiH, to the extent they did not need to fear return fire and was able to leave its mortars in permanent positions. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think you're wrong -- I don't think you're right. I think you have wrong information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What artillery pieces were there on that part of the confrontation lines that you've told us about? What type of weapons? What guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On which side do you mean? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On your side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the rear of my positions, there was one artillery unit which had 100-millimetre cannons. They were anti-tank cannons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you at any stage between September 1992 and August 1994 go to the Lukavica headquarters of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever travel to the southern front of the conflict, that is, on the southern side of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you travel to the end of the left flank of the Romanija Brigade at any stage in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not in connection with carrying out military tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO could pan back in relation to the exhibit which is presently on it. A bit further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, could you point to the furthest point of the confrontation line which was the responsibility of the Romanija Brigade on the left flank. What was the endpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't point. I don't know about that. I don't know about the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the battalion. I'm asking you about the end of responsibility on the left flank for your brigade, the brigade that you were in throughout the conflict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I don't know the endpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. This is several times that this question is asked successively, although the witness has answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I disagree with that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just rereading the questions and the answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP20 -- first of all, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the question in different forms has been put, or at least information is sought from the witness. The Chamber cannot see that it's properly answered several times. You told us that you went to the western end of your brigade's confrontation line, but it was not for duty reasons. So I take it it was either for private reasons or anything else. Could you tell us where the end of the brigade line may have been, where that was? Could you indicate that on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there's a misunderstanding. We didn't mention the western part. If I point to the -- this, I think you mean this is western. Are we thinking of the same thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution was asking about left and right. I took it, but please correct me, Mr. Ierace, when I'm wrong, that if you're talking about the left side of the line, that you are talking about the left side as seen from the positions of the Serbian forces, and that would mean just --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Just the other part of the line, Mr. DP20. So Mr. Ierace is asking you about the end of the line, I would say closer to the word "Sarajevo" on the map. From your position facing the opposite forces, the left-hand side of the line, where did it end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. In that part, I don't know exactly where the line ended. I went for private reasons up to the place called Miljevci, because I have relatives there and I went to visit them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The line as you have drawn it for your area of responsibility extends a little distance between the name "Sarajevo" in large type. Were you familiar with where the front line went from that point, further south or southwest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was familiar with a small part which is directly linked to my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You're taking out the pen. Don't mark it. Please point to the end of the SRK front line, the left flank. Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't point to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, please point to the end of the line that you have marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a line of one battalion from the brigade of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, and is that the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you know where the line went from that point? And please keep the pointer on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You indicate a distance of a few centimetres. Is that as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know for sure. I'd rather not...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So effectively, you have very little knowledge as to where the front line went beyond the length that you operated on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in terms of artillery, so far you've told us about one piece that was operating in relation to that marked section of the front line. Surely there was more than that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us again, firstly, how many pieces of artillery there were, let's say, in December 1992 in the vicinity or behind --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How does the witness know that? The witness said that in terms of artillery, in relation to artillery, he was in the infantry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but he told us about... The objection is denied. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A few moments ago when I asked you about -- I asked you what artillery resources operated in relation to that part of the front line, had you told us about an anti-tank gun. Do you recollect that, telling us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Were there times when you requested artillery assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for artillery support from the commander of the battalion, and they continued on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to consult my Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Should the witness wait outside, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask to put the microphone off. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Galic has asked of me to stress in relation to the objection that I made earlier, is that it would be good to say with regard to the competence of the witness, that he was not -- nothing more than a platoon commander, and that he couldn't have had the technical capacity for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the objection has been raised. The objection has been denied. There's no further discussion on that. And I'll perhaps at a later stage discuss this way of operating in more detail. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you requested artillery support from your battalion, do you know where that support came from? Where was the artillery that provided it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know precisely about the artillery from the battalion. These were 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you include 120-millimetre mortars under the heading "artillery." I'm more interested in guns, field guns, Howitzers, perhaps even tanks; that type of artillery. Where did that come from when you requested it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From these positions that I told you about. Behind us, there were positions of an artillery unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, to be clear on this, when you say there were positions behind you of artillery units, do you mean artillery other than mortars, not mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Did you sometimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President -- I'll withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you sometimes see those artillery pieces between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see ammunition near them, shells stacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there corps artillery placed adjacent to, that is, behind the front line that you operated on, artillery that came from the corps command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the corps command. There was an independent artillery unit which was subordinated to the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please point to where that was in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please take a pen, that's the blue pen, place a cross indicating that position, and alongside write the letters "CA."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, what was that artillery in that position in December 1992? Field guns or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were anti-armour cannons, 100-millimetre anti-tank guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there near it an UNMO position, UNMO Lima, that is United Nations Military Observers' position, in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were observers, because they controlled that artillery unit but I don't know what their exact location was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see gentlemen in -- with blue helmets in that vicinity at any stage, that position you just marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand that they were United Nations Military Observers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice in that position shells stacked near the guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The other day, you marked on the map the position of the battalion headquarters. Would you now please mark on the map the position of the brigade headquarters as of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part of the map that I have before me, I'm not able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We're talking about the headquarters of your brigade, the Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place alongside that circle "BEH." Thank you. Letters "BEH."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown P3727, in particular, map 5, and he continue to have in front of him the present exhibit. At the moment, could we have on the ELMO the map that has just been obtained, that is P3727. And could the map be lowered a little, draw the map down so that we can see higher up the map. Thank you. Perhaps that's a little too far. Perhaps the map could be moved up. Thank you. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, I want you to take your time and look carefully at the position of the dark green broken line on this map. I want you to look at the names which appear on that map. Sorry. Can you please tell us when you've done that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In relation to the area that you operated on, is it correct? In other words, does the green line indicate the front line between the two opposing forces, that part of it on which you operated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please wait for a minute. I don't want to mislead you. The dark green line indicates the forward position of the ABiH. And take your time and tell us if you agree that in relation to the area you knew well, it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. So that's accurate, the part that you knew well, that you operated on, in terms of forward positions of the ABiH. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. I can't see well on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you now look at the map that you marked, D1789, and compare them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are slight differences. Hrastova Glavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to Hrastova Glavica on the map. Just keep your pointer there while we adjust the ELMO so we can see where you're pointing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I think you now point to the name Hrastova Glavica which appears on the map. You point to the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the position passed through the peak, the highest peak, that's above Hrastova Glavica. There should be a number, a trig point here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I draw your attention more to the north point of the front line that you are familiar with. In particular, do you see on this map Barice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please leave the pointer, if you would for a minute, on that position. Please leave it there until I ask you to move it. Thank you. And I think that name actually appears on the map. Can you read it? Do you see Barice where you are pointing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barice, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, to the right, do you see Odjak or Odzak, to the right of pointer. And if so, would you now point at that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. With the assistance of Mr. Usher, perhaps we can now have the other map, D1789, on the ELMO. Would you please point to Barice on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And now, Odzak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might, for the moment, D -- those two maps be returned. I'll come back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't follow you. Could you point to that place again. Please point at that place again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Barice. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, whilst Your Honours are looking at the maps, to save time, I'd be grateful if Madam Registrar could prepare maps 8 and 3 of Exhibit P3728. That's the other set of maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although we are looking on the maps, we are ready to hear the next questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Please leave the map on the ELMO for the moment. And could the ELMO pan back. And stop panning back at that point. If the map could be moved so we can see -- withdraw that. Could the map be moved slightly to the right. Slightly higher, higher. The other direction. Stop. And could we now zoom in. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you firstly look at the map in front of you, and as blown up on the screen. Do you see Grdonj? And if so, would you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you please slowly move the pointer along the ABiH front line that you have marked on that. The ABiH front line, not the SRK front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. And now we see that you have not marked the ABiH line in relation to the longitude of Grdonj, but where you have marked it, which is to the north-east, it is some distance north of Grdonj, is that correct, that is, the ABiH front line? Do you agree with that, the nearest part that you've marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm claiming that the line was where I marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Now, firstly, would you look again at the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's for the record P3727. And perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On this map, would you please point to Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we have had the experience earlier that a specific name several times on the same map quite close to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President. To overcome that problem, might that map be removed and might the witness be shown P3728, number 3. Perhaps I could have a look at it before it's shown to the witness. Yes, thank you. All right. Now, could the ELMO please pan back a little. And the map be moved slightly to the right. Thank you. And could we have the light on on the ELMO. Has the bulb blown? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see firstly on this map Sedam Suma, which I think is Seven Woods. That is, the name Sedam Suma. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness now points to that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that there's a light-green line that passes through Suma on that map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness now points to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I want you to understand that I'm suggesting to you that light-green line shows the position of the ABiH forward positions or forward line, front line. Do you understand what I'm putting to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand that, but I don't agree that that's the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Okay. In relation to the other line, we see a dark-green line, and then a blue line. Would you please point to the dark-green broken line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please point to the blue line, hand-marked blue line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to suggest to you that the -- I'll withdraw. Do you see Grdonj indicated on this map immediately above and partly through the dark-blue line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. And indeed, Sedam Suma, as I understand it, is to the south of Grdonj. Is that correct? I'm not asking you about the lines for the moment, just whether Sedam Suma is to the south of Grdonj, the peak of Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I suggest to you that as of mid-1993, indeed, at least from April 1993 to August 1993, the blue line indicates the forward position of the SRK in relation to Grdonj. If you don't know whether it did, please say so. If you do know, do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. The line should be further to the rear. It should go in the direction of the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. The Defence has, with regard to incident number 3, an entire set of maps, and for incident number 3, the front line of both armies is completely different. It also says "incident number 3." Perhaps I've made a mistake, but I'm under the impression that it is the same incident, but that the line has been drawn in a different manner. This is confusing me and my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could I please have a look at... Ms. Pilipovic, may I first ask you, the map we're using now is admitted into evidence as far as I'm aware of you and you now confront us with a map which bears no number, neither a P nor a D number, and which is --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I said that I apologise, but I have a complete set here. I took it from the complete set of maps that I received. This is what's confusing me because I thought that the maps were the same regardless of the fact that I'm aware of the fact that this map has been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the -- the Prosecution is entitled to put to the witness a map, and even if it differs from a map that exists somewhere else, but that it could create confusion is quite clear. Perhaps the parties could, not in the presence of the witness, see whether they can explain to each other what one map is and what the purpose of using this map perhaps rather than another map is. And I'll return this now to you, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed. I think the last answer of the witness was that the line indicated on the map you showed him, Mr. Ierace, was not the right one. It should be more in the rear, more to the north as far as I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, what we're talking about in this area is Spicasta Stijena. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The area immediately to the right of Grdonj where we see a grown line and a red arrow, I'm sorry, a green line and a red circle is known as Spicasta Stijena, isn't it? Sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that feature does exist. It is there, but this map is not very detailed, so I couldn't say that it is at this exact point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Grdonj, the highest point, is the southernmost end of an escarpment. As one looks at the map to the right, the escarpment extends to the northeast. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I explain to you what this feature looks like in nature? On the basis of this, I can't see it now. I don't know how the rock or feature has been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Recognising features on the map. Leave the map to one side. If you could look at me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. I'm also looking at the clock, if you would find a suitable moment for a break. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: This may be an appropriate moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed. If there's any issue outstanding on the basis of your discussions during the break, we would like to hear it. But then of course we would like to hear whether it's a disclosure issue or what type of issue it is, because until now as far as my recollection goes, I have never seen that before. But I might be mistaken. But the map Ms. Pilipovic just showed, it's without a number; it's not my recollection that we ever admitted into evidence or that it was ever tendered into evidence. Up until now, it's not a problem which the Chamber should occupy itself, I take it. If that would be different, then we'll hear from the parties. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a map to be shown to the witness. Perhaps I could provide a copy to Madam Registrar. And the number will be P3755. I have a number of copies. Mr. President, I could indicate where that map has come from, or perhaps I should do it in the absence of the witness at a later point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a map we have seen before, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not, then perhaps you'll explain it in the absence of the witness. Mr. DP20, may I ask you to leave the courtroom just for a while. You'll be escorted by the usher. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a section of a map that we have received from the Defence. The map is titled in Cyrillic "working map of headquarters," and it's dated the 1st of July, 1994. It was given to us in sections. And it was given to us on the 10th of September, 2002. I don't know that we have all the sections, but we have at least this section. And I intend to show it to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the witness comes in, could we please have several -- there are several sections of the map, so could we please have on the first page an indication of the map so that we know what this is about, because there are several sections, several elements. Could we please be given this initial reference so that we know who has made this map, why and how, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it assists, I have the two A4 sections which have them on the title of the map. And I think -- yes, the date as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you have a copy, to give it to the Defence. Mr. Ierace, have these sections been used before? It's not clear in my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not that I remember, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So they are new for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: They may have been, but I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please give that to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And just in the absence of the witness, if it assists in general understanding, the map that's presently on the ELMO was marked by General Karavelic. He placed the blue line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. DP20. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown the map which is P3755, and might be it be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, please look at that map, and if you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the one. That one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you can find it, please point to Grdonj as it appears on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could the map be moved slightly to the left. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the name "Grdonj."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please point to Barice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. And Odzak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness points to -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And also would you now please point to Sedrenik as it appears on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness has now pointed to those four places as the names are indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I want you to assume that the thick dotted line, or line consisting of dashes, indicates the forward positions of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. And the thinner broken line underneath indicates the forward positions of the ABiH. And I want you to assume that these positions are as of the 1st of July, 1994. Do you understand what I have just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I want you to assume that the two lines indicate the forward positions of the opposing armies as of the 1st of July, 1994. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, I want to point out some differences between these forward positions and those that you marked on the map the other day, which for the transcript is D1789. I think you still have the map that you marked on the table in front of you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You marked the forward positions of the SRK, basically passing through Barice and Odzak, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On this map, we see that the forward positions of the SRK were a considerable distance to the south of those two towns, don't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are not towns. These are small villages. And considering the difference in the scale of these two maps, I think that's right. I can't say it's a hundred per cent correct, but I think that they are in accordance with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that in relation to the villages of Barice and Odzak, they are clearly in conflict with each other.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please place on the ELMO with the assistance of the usher map D1789.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, so that we can understand things in a better way, could Mr. Ierace indicate the scale of the map that he has just produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, is that a copy of the map as you received it, or have you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- enlarged it or it's the scale in which the Defence provided it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any indication of the scale? If it's enlarged, it doesn't help very much, unless there is a -- apart from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. numbers, if there is also a scale indicated on the map itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it would take some time for us to check if there is a scale indicated, but my fundamental response is that we don't need that because we can see the relevant towns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, but if the parties could give some clarifications as to the scale at a later stage. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you say anything, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'd like to hear from you what the Defence has to tell us. There should be no indications in whatever way of what is the view of the General and what is the view of Defence counsel. I wanted to leave this for a later moment, but you are not supposed to indicate whose views you're expressing. It's the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I must correct something I've just said. I have just been informed that the map has been slightly enlarged from the original image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that the scale is approximately 1 square, that is, the side of one square, equals 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's exactly what I wanted to say before I was being told off about respecting the rules. I believe the first rule is when the maps are enlarged, and asking leading questions of a witness, it would be good to tell the opposing side of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, would you point again Barice on the map that you marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO could be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Sir, you have the SRK front line passing alongside, first of all, the name "Barice" on the map immediately underneath it, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, is the village indicated by a series of dots to the right and slightly below that name on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did the SRK line pass on the southern boundary of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, indeed, when you marked the front line, you seem to have followed a black line, a straight line, that was already on the map. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly, yes. That was a line indicating a long-distance power line, but not all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the point that the power lines passed immediately south of the village of Barice, according to your markings, that was the forward position of the SRK. Correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, please point again to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, the line passes immediately to the south of dots indicating the village of Odzak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The line on the other map, 3755, and perhaps you can place that back on the ELMO, is different in that it is significantly further south of those two villages, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. As long as the scale and the enlargement are not known, I don't think we can conclude anything whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you perhaps leave out the word "considerably" because that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please run the pointer along the power line as indicated on this map where it traverses the southern edge of the village of Barice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And continue to trace that line to the right as it passes alongside the southern area of the village of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you drew that line, you started off to the right, and moved your pen to the left on the other map. And as you approached Odzak and Barice, the front line rose to the left. On this map, as we move along the indicated front line, it drops as you move to the left. In other words, the front line dips to the south. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which map do you mean. The first or the second? What I've marked or what's on the other map marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The map which is on the ELMO at the moment, which for the transcript is 3755. Do you see if you start at the right edge of that map the power line goes up to the left and the front lines dip down to the left, that is, they dip south. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. You now indicate the front line moving south as the pointer moves from the left to the right. That is a significant difference, sir, isn't it, in your recollection of the front line and the front line as it appears on this map in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to compare. I think this, this feature, Pasina Brdo, I used this as a reference point, and this was under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you told us what you used as a reference were the power lines, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this is where the power lines go because I know the area very well. And this line represents the power line which was in existence then. It doesn't exist today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you a very simple question. Do you agree that there is a significant difference in the front-line positions as you marked them on the one hand, and as they appear on the map in front of you now, 3755, on the other hand in the area between Sedrenik and Barice and Odzak? Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree because of the scale of the map, I can see that these are insignificant differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. Now, I'd like to point out to you another difference, I suggest, between these two maps. Look first at the map that you marked, and do you see how as we move from the right to the left the distance between the two front lines becomes greater in the vicinity of Odzak, as you move from left to right past Amerovice [phoen]. To the left, we see a bulge in the gap, between the two front lines. Do you see that? Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What do you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see a town or village in the area between the two front lines called H-L-A-D-I-V-O-D-E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You now point to that town. And the way you have it, that's in no man's land. That's between the front lines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. At that point, the distance between the front lines is far greater than it is where the name in large type "Sarajevo" appears. Do you agree? Please point to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. As we follow with our eye the front lines travelling Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. north and to the left, the distance between them becomes greater as you have marked them on this map. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You agree, all right. Now, please look at the other map. 3755.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If the ELMO could be zoomed back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the same area, do you agree that the distance between the front lines remains approximately constant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, on this map, would you again point to Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the assistance of Mr. Usher, perhaps we could zoom in on Grdonj. Could we now zoom in, and the map has to be raised up. Thank you. If we can keep going as far as we can. Map could be raised up. Stop there, please. Thank you. Back a little so we can focus. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you see on this map what appear to be the letters "CP" above Grdonj? You might see it more clearly on your screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see any letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right, do you see a "P" at least?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right. Do you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we wanted to be able to follow, and I have to admit that these Cs and Ps are confusing us. I don't really know what the Prosecution is talking about. If they could be clearer, it would be good for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, where you asked the witness to recognise a C and a P, I had some difficulties both on my screen and on the map to find anything like that. So the witness might have the same problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it handwriting or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know, because this is the way it has come into our possession, and I'm not sure it does say CP, and that's why I used the words "what appears to be CP." And I accept what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place your pointer on the portion of the map that we see in the screen, in particular on the southernmost part of the road on which we see Grdonj. Would you place your pointer on the map so that we can see your pointer on the screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you place it on the road above Grdonj, the end of the road above Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please keep the pointer still on the end of the other road, the road above Grdonj, not to the left of Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace is asking you to put your pointer a bit more to the right, a bit more up. A bit more to the right. That road on the end of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right, please leave your pointer there. Now, have you ever travelled on that road, ever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the Dayton agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I take it you did not travel on that road before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And when you went there after the Dayton agreement, to the right of the road -- withdraw that. Did you leave the road and walk around the area at the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. The witness said that he used this road after the Dayton agreement, and this concerns the chronology, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Whether he visited that area after the Dayton agreement and whether he went around there. Is that understanding correct? Yes. So the objection is based on a misunderstanding of the question. The question was, Mr. DP20, whether you left the road and walked around when you visited that road after the Dayton agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I only drove down it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why did you drive down it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was going to Mrkovici, because it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, where were you going, to where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, that's a dead-end road, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You see on the map it appears to be a dead-end road, that is, the section which extends in a southwesterly direction towards the name Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you that there is a road here, but I don't know when this map was made, in which year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the map could be moved -- kept still. Thank you. Now, you said you were going to Mrkovici. Where were you coming from on this occasion after the Dayton Peace Agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And when you say you were travelling --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection concerning the relevance of the questions. The relevance of the question with regard to the events we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. Questions could have some relevance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, when you travelled up to Mrkovici, did you take the road that we see on the screen that goes to the left, runs north/south, and goes to the left of the name Barice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. That's the road. It goes by the Grdonj peak. It goes by it, and then continues on towards Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, the part that goes by the Grdonj peak, as you gave that answer, you were indicating coming from the left of Grdonj. Were you travelling on a road which does not appear on this map as you approached the area of Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that exact road is marked on the map because I know that this is a fairly recent road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And is it a dirt road, the section which does not appear on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macadam road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now to the right of Grdonj, just above Sedrenik, can you see a road that if you follow with the eye would lead you to the same intersection with Grdonj. Would you please point to the road above Sedrenik, immediately above Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you see that on the map that road snakes at radical angles backwards and forwards? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you want me to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you agree that the road as it appears on the map between Sedrenik and Grdonj snakes to the left and to the right, turns sharply to the left and to the right immediately above Sedrenik. Bring your pointer back down to the area of road immediately above Sedrenik. Thank you. Do you see the road move sharply to the left and to the right. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It does that because there is a steep slope at that point, doesn't it, as you come from Sedrenik driving away from Sedrenik, you are rising sharply, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And from Sedrenik, where the name appears, if you looked to the northwest, you would be looking at an escarpment, wouldn't you, a ridgeline? No, not the northeast, the northwest. Perhaps you could place your pointer to the northwest of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. You're now indicating to the northwest. Now further up the road towards Grdonj. Stop there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please keep your pointer still. I suggest that exactly where you have your pointer, there is an escarpment, a ridge. What do you say to that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I suggest to you that the -- along the edge of the top of the escarpment were SRK trenches. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the ABiH territory went as far as the bottom of the escarpment. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More to the rear, not on the escarpment itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, below the escarpment. The ABiH at the bottom; the SRK at the top. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the claim concerning our line is correct. But the ABiH positions were more in the direction of Sedrenik, so not on the escarpment itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not saying they were on the escarpment, I'm saying they were at the bottom, but we'll leave there. Now, if you imagine standing around Sedrenik and looking to the northwest, if you followed the escarpment along to the left, then eventually you would find yourself looking at the end of the ridge where Grdonj was. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now before we leave this map, let's see if we can agree on this: According to the map in front of you now, 3755, the forward positions of the SRK ended somewhere south of the end of the marked road. Do you agree with that, according to this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to repeat that again. This is like the previous image, the positions were a little to the north. A little further north.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Listen to the question. Do you agree that according to this map, SRK positions were somewhere to the south, not too far, but somewhere to the south of the end of the road which we see above Grdonj, in particular, above the "J" on Grdonj. We see the line between the top of the J and the end of that road. Perhaps you can point to it. Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now go back to the other map, the map you marked. Now, with the assistance of Mr. Usher, can we have a close-up of the same portion of this map, that is, the end of the road. So we have to move the map to the left and upwards. Sorry, the other way. Higher. Perhaps, if we pan back first. And if you could move the map in the other direction, that is, to the right, not to the left. Other direction. Further, further. Stop. A bit further to the right. I'm sorry, the other way. Yes. Up, so that we can see. Thank you. If we could zoom in. Move it a bit further so that we can see further down. Thank you. Stop there. That will do. Now, will you please point to the end of the road as it appears on this map. Please point to the end of the road. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you see that a short distance south of the end of the road we see the symbol for trig station and the altitude reading 906. Do you see that? I don't know whether trig station translates. Do you see a peak indicated with the numbers 906?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I have to admit that I do not know what a trig station is. It seems to be a technical term. Could you explain what that is for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The easiest way would be to avoid it. It's a high point. It's a map reference point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, does that accord with your knowledge that just south of that road is the highest point, and perhaps we can accept from the map that that altitude is 906 metres. Do you agree with what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this narrow area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Listen to the question carefully. First of all, place your pointer on the end of the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just south of the end of the road, do you see the number, and slightly to the right, under beneath your pointer, do you see the numbers "906"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The high point of that area was immediately south of the end of that road and had that altitude. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: According to the other map, the forward position of the SRK was somewhere south of the end of the road near your pointer, that is, the end of the road that we can see near your pointer. That's correct, isn't it, according to the other map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but it's difficult for me to compare these two maps and to accept to compare them because there are quite a lot of differences. As far as the scale is concerned, the scale is larger here. And the small scale that's used for the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Listen, please, carefully to the question. On this map, we see the same road, don't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And leaving aside the question of scale, the SRK position, according to the other map, was somewhere south of the end of the road you just pointed to, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this map, yes. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that according to this map, yes. But in my opinion, there are certain differences here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the actual situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit P3728, number 3 again, please. Mr. President, I only have a question or two to go on this issue. And if we could pan back and zoom in on Grdonj as it appears on this map. If Mr. Usher could manoeuvre the map -- thank you, that will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, do you see the numbers 906 on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you see a symbol -- withdraw that. And according to this map, the front line of the SRK -- withdraw that. Do you see what you would accept to be a symbol indicating that high point? Yes or no. If you don't, please say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you see a dotted line above Grdonj and slightly to the right in a yellowish colour? Perhaps you could point to it. Further up, a broken line, perhaps indicating a road. Further up and to the right. Higher and to the right. Please move your pointer higher and to the right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, let's assume for the moment that that line indicates the same road that we saw earlier. Do you agree with me that the position of the SRK front lines, according to this map, is consistent at this point with map 3755; that is, the small map that you saw a few moments ago? The positions are about the same, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, sir, the first time I had a look at this map, I said that I didn't agree with this line, that it had to go further to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for your opinion as to where the line should be; I'm only asking you whether you agree that the markings on the map are consistent as to the forward positions of the SRK. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You disagree. All right. And perhaps one more question, Mr. President, or one more issue. Now we see on the screen the red circle. Do you remember I suggested to you earlier that that red circle was on the escarpment? Do you now agree that indeed that indicates a position approximately that was on top of the escarpment where you told us earlier there were SRK trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I think it should be a little more to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could review it overnight, Mr. President. There were some issues, and other issues which came up unexpectedly. Could I indicate a more reliable time, a reliable time, tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that does not mean that the Chamber will follow your indication, but of course if you could perhaps in the absence of the witness tell us tomorrow what issues you'd like to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, in the absence of the witness, could I just have a minute to record something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. DP20, we'll adjourn for today. We'll continue tomorrow morning, 9.00. I hope it will not take too much time tomorrow. I'll ask Mr. Usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. I'll ask for the patience of the interpreters. Mr. Ierace promised us it would take one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the commission of experts’ two documents, yesterday and today, the Defence was asked what was the relevance. Today on page 7, line 19, Mr. Piletta-Zanin said: "Mr. President, just to specify, the 24th is a very special day for a specific incident when other witnesses said there was no combat." That was a very revealing comment because it meant when one looks at the scheduled sniping incidents that the two documents in fact relate to two scheduled sniping incidents. No mention was made in the 65 ter summaries of this witness saying anything at all about any scheduled sniping incidents, nor was anything said about him referring to any scheduled shelling incidents. And again this witness was asked about the characteristics of 120-millimetre mortars which are clearly relevant to incident 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've already told the Defence that it should have been in the summary, or it should have been updated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, the last one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does the Defence want to respond, also in one minute?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes. We'll respond willingly. The Defence has already had the occasion to say what is important, that's the truth. And we have noticed that sometimes the truth comes out unpredictably. But that's not a reason not to reveal it. When we spoke about weapons with this witness, and this was the case with the previous witness, we were concerned with the same thing, the type, et cetera. In the case of this witness, we didn't specify this because the hearing was in progress and we didn't think it was useful to reproach him for what he said about the 120 millimetres and the craters, I don't think this has a basis. But for the other witnesses, we will now provide far more detail about what other military witnesses are going to say. I have already said that all these witness can testify with regard to craters. Thank you. And when I say craters, I mean big and small craters, et cetera. All these military witnesses will be able to be called to testify about craters, and specifically about 120-millimetre craters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will consider the matter. It is important, as I told before to the Defence, that in respect of the fairness of the trial, that the other party should be able to identify specific issues. If you indicate, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that all the witnesses will tell us about 120-millimetre craters, then of course another aspect arises whether we have to expect repetitious evidence. But we'll have to consider it -- we'll listen to you, and you know exactly what the Chamber expects the Defence to do in respect of informing the Prosecution. We'll adjourn -- one moment, please. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 1.49 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
